title: Rosalind and the Signal
premise: Elodie Whitlock, a disgraced navigator flying contraband memory-backups of the dead between quarantined worlds, has spent nine years staying invisible on the long route. When the salvage ship Meridian returns from deep space with its crew aged backward into children who remember their own deaths, Elodie recognizes the anomaly: it matches the backups in his hold, which were copied from a signal no one should have survived. Pursued by the Charter's enforcers and shadowed by the child-crew who insist he was there when they died, Elodie races to the relay at the edge of dead space, where he must decide whether to destroy the signal, broadcast the truth that will shatter the Charter's quarantine, or feed the backups back into it and resurrect the dead at the cost of the living. He chooses the truth, dies in the relay's light, and wakes—as a memory in someone else's hold, finally at peace with being remembered.
about_author: Bram Halloran is the pen name of a former merchant marine radio officer who spent a decade on tramp freighters before turning to fiction. He writes slow, aching science fiction about people who keep the lights on at the edge of things.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Establishing his quiet, illegal life: navigating the Kestrel between quarantined colonies, smuggling memory-backups of the dead to families who refuse to let go. He checks on the hold's sleeping backups like a night nurse. Emotional beat: tender melancholy and the discipline of not looking back.

chapters.title: Cargo That Dreams
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A client, Ilsa Voss, receives her dead son's backup and asks Elodie the question he dreads: does it dream? He lies. A Charter patrol skims the port, forcing a hasty departure. Emotional beat: guilt sharpening into fear that his cargo is not cargo at all.

chapters.title: Meridian, Returning
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Docking at Thessaly Ring, he witnesses the salvage ship Meridian arrive after nine years lost in dead space—its crew of forty now children, biologically reversed, screaming in unison when the port lights come on. Emotional beat: horror and a terrible flicker of recognition.

chapters.title: The Children Who Remember Dying
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A child named Tam grabs Elodie's sleeve and says, 'You were on the bridge. You let us go.' Elodie has never met the Meridian. Charter enforcers quarantine the ship and everyone who touched it. Emotional beat: denial cracking under the weight of a child's certainty.

chapters.title: What the Hold Keeps
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Alone aboard the Kestrel, he audits his backups and finds one he cannot account for: a woman's pattern, nine years old, with metadata stamped from inside dead space. He plays thirty seconds of her and hears his own voice. Emotional beat: vertigo—his past is not what he remembers.

chapters.title: Nine Years Ago
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, Elodie and the unknown woman's recovered memory-fragments. Flashback: the survey ship Cassiopeia entered the dead-space relay and found a signal that rewrites time locally; Elodie was navigator; something happened on the bridge. His memory ends at an airlock. Emotional beat: the horror of a missing hour.

chapters.title: The Charter Comes Aboard
chapters.summary: Enforcer POV (Inspector Rhea Sol). Sol boards the Kestrel hunting the Cassiopeia's black box, which the Charter buried nine years ago. She finds Elodie's backup hold and realizes he is not a smuggler—he is the sole survivor the Charter erased. Emotional beat: cat-and-mouse with sympathy on both sides.

chapters.title: Running the Quarantine Line
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. He burns his moorings and jumps the cordon with the child-crew stowing away aboard—Tam insists the signal is calling them home. Sol pursues but hesitates at the firing solution. Emotional beat: found-family forming in the worst possible circumstances.

chapters.title: Ages Running Backward
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. The children age backward another year during the jump; Tam's adult memories are dissolving into a child's grammar. She teaches Elodie the Meridian's last coordinates before she loses them. Emotional beat: grief for a self that is being unwritten.

chapters.title: The Man in the Relay Records
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Decrypted relay logs show the Charter knew about the signal for nine years and used it to make the dead's backups—a resurrection industry built on a time anomaly. Elodie's hold was a distribution node. He was complicit. Emotional beat: loyalty to his clients curdling into complicity.

chapters.title: Ilsa Voss's Son
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV, with intercut messages. He realizes the backup he delivered in chapter 2 will eventually reverse-age its recipient's family the way the Meridian's crew was reversed. The signal gives life and takes it back with interest. Emotional beat: the cost of mercy.

chapters.title: Sol Catches Up
chapters.summary: Sol's POV. She corners the Kestrel at a fuel ghost-station but instead of arresting Elodie, she shows him her own file: her brother's backup is in his hold. She has been hunting the signal to get him back. Emotional beat: enemies discovering they want the same impossible thing.

chapters.title: The Bargain at the Ghost Station
chapters.summary: Dual POV, Elodie and Sol. Uneasy alliance: she'll get them through the Charter's inner cordon if Elodie promises her brother's pattern back. Elodie knows delivering it may kill her. He promises anyway. Emotional beat: the seduction of a lie you want to be true.

chapters.title: Through the Inner Cordon
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A tense, silent run through Charter minefields, the child-crew singing to steady the navigation—their backward-aging brains somehow resonating with the signal's mathematics. Elodie realizes the children are an antenna. Emotional beat: awe and dread braided together.

chapters.title: What Tam Forgets
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam has regressed to age six and can no longer remember why they're flying, only that the man at the helm is safe. She gives Elodie her last adult artifact: a data-chit with the Meridian's final log. Emotional beat: innocence as both loss and gift.

chapters.title: The Meridian's Last Log
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The log shows the truth: the Cassiopeia's crew didn't die—they were folded into the signal, and the Charter's backups are echoes of the living dead. Elodie's missing hour: he chose to stay outside the fold and has hated himself for it ever since. Emotional beat: shame transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Edge of Dead Space
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The Kestrel reaches the relay at the boundary of dead space. The signal is no longer broadcasting—it's waiting. The backups in the hold wake and speak with one voice: come back, finish what you started. Emotional beat: the threshold, and the pull of every easy answer.

chapters.title: Three Doors
chapters.summary: Elodie and Sol, dual POV. At the relay, three options crystallize: destroy the signal and the backups forever; broadcast the truth and collapse the Charter's quarantine economy; or enter the fold and restore the dead at the risk of the living. Sol demands her brother. Elodie refuses to choose for everyone alone. Emotional beat: the loneliness of the deciding vote.

chapters.title: The Vote of the Small
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. The children, asked what they want, choose the truth—not resurrection, not silence. 'We already died,' Tam says. 'Tell them we died.' Elodie's loyalty to his clients, Sol's to her brother, both bend against the children's clarity. Emotional beat: the youngest voices carrying the heaviest wisdom.

chapters.title: Climax: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The Charter fleet arrives as Elodie threads the Kestrel into the relay and uploads everything—the signal, the logs, the backups, his own missing hour—to every world at once. Sol lets it happen, choosing truth over her brother. The relay ignites. Emotional beat: sacrifice as the only honest act left.

chapters.title: After the Light
chapters.summary: Sol's POV. The Charter's resurrection economy collapses; quarantines fall; the Meridian's children, freed from the signal's resonance, finally begin aging forward again. Sol holds Elodie's backup pattern—the only one she saved—and cannot decide whether waking it is mercy or theft. Emotional beat: grief and gratitude inseparable.

chapters.title: Rosalind and the Signal
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Tam's POV, years later. Tam, grown again, pilots a small honest ship and carries one backup in her hold: Elodie's, named Rosalind—the woman from the hold, who was the signal's first folded voice, and who carried Elodie's pattern home. She wakes her. Emotional beat: memory as the truest form of loyalty.
